ROAD ACCIDENTS DUE TO ENGINEERING DEFECTS IN NHS 
 
2752. SHRI UPENDRA SINGH RAWAT: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of road accidents registered during the last three years 
and the current year due  to road engineering defects, State/UT -
wise, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and other metro cities; 
(b)  whether the Government has taken up initiatives to restructure and 
strengthen road safety and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c)  whether the Government has allocated funds for the purpose and if 
so, these details of expenditure  incurred thereon, State/UT -wise, 
particularly in Uttar Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a)     With a view to providing relevant and reliable data on accidents, 
Transport Research Wing (TRW) under the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways collects and compiles accident data from the police 
departments of all States/UTs. However, TRW does not compile road 
accidents data on the basis of road engineering defects. 
(b)     Major initiatives taken by the Ministry based on road engineering 
to restructure and strengthen road safety in the country are as under : - 
  
(i)  Ministry has issued guidelines for conduct of safety audits at all 
stages (design, construction, and operation). 
 
(ii)  Road safety audit policy has been issued by National Highways 
Authority of India (NHAI) on 27.05.2022 prescribing Audit 
requirements as per IRC guidelines in all phase of the project. 
 

(iii)  Road safety audit is an integral part of detailed project report (DPR) 
/ feasibility study as per IRC guidelines and action is being taken by 
Ministry accordingly in all projects. 
 
(iv)  Third party independent road safety audit at DPR stage has been 
made mandatory by NHAI. 
 
(v)  Ministry, vide OM No. RW/NH -29011/2/2015/P&M (RSCE) dated 7th 
December 2015, has issued guidelines on “Preparation and 
submission of proposals for rectification of identified road accident 
black spots on National Highways (NHs)”. 
 
(vi)  Ministry, vide circul ar no. RW/NH -29013/01/2020 - S&R dated 09th 
November 2020, has issued Guidelines, for monitoring of and 
compliance of all safety and suggested procedures, to be followed 
for preparation of proposal for rectification of Black Spots. 
 
(vii) Ministry, vide le tter no.  RW/NH-29011/01/2021-S&R (P&B) RSCE 
dated 9th Sept 2021, has also issued guidelines for taking advance 
action for removal of accident spots on NHs as per police reports 
without waiting for converting them into black spots after 
accidents/fatalities. 
 
(viii)Regular review meetings are conducted by senior officers of ministry 
with Regional/field officers of all road owning agencies related to 
NHs to formulate action plans for identification and rectification of 
black spots and accident spots with a targeted Timeline. 
  
(c)     Ministry has conveyed the sanction ceiling of Rs. 1200 Crore during 
financial year 2022-23 for road safety works, primarily for taking up the 
rectification of blackspots. State wise details are in the table below:-

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS

ANSWERED ON 22ND DECEMBER, 2022 
ELECTRONIC MONITORING SYSTEM ON NHS 
 
2755. SHRI RAJ KUMAR CHAHAR: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that overspeeding  is the major 
reason for road accidents and it can be curbed by electronic 
monitoring and follow up challans and if so, the reaction of the 
Government in this regard; 
(b)  the present status of electronic monitoring system on the National 
Highways (NHs);  
(c)  the initiatives taken by the Government for electronic monitoring 
of NHs and time frame for ensuring full compliance of the legal 
requirements of the Motor Vehicle Act in this regard; and 
(d)  the number of traffic personnel in the country as required  against 
the total length of NHs? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (d)    Based on the FIR data received from various States/UTs, the 
yearly analysis are carried out by Transport Research Wing of this 
Ministry. Road accident deaths occur due to multiple causes such 
as over speeding, use of Mobile phone, drunken driving/c onsumption of 
alcohol / drug, overloaded Vehicle, vehicular condition, poor light 
condition, jumping red light, overtaking, neglect of civic bodies, weather 
condition, fault of driver, driving on wrong side, defect in road condition, 
defect in condition of  motor vehicle, fault of cyclist, fault of pedestrian 
etc.  
The role of Central Government is to notify the regulations under the 
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. 
Further, the responsibility of implementation of the regulations as framed 
by the Central Government lies with the States/UTs. 

For Electronic Monitoring, Ministry has inserted new Section 
136A “Electronic monitoring and enforcement of road safety” as per 
Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019. 
   Ministry has notified rules for Electronic Monitoring and Enforcement 
of Road Safety vide G.S.R. 575(E) dated 11th August, 2021. The rules 
specify the detailed provisions for placement of electronic enforcement 
devices (speed camera, closed -circuit television camera, speed gun , 
body wearable camera, dashboard camera, Automatic Number Plate 
Recognition (ANPR), weigh in machine (WIM) and any such other 
technology specified by the State Government). State Governments shall 
ensure that appropriate electronic enforcement devices are  placed at 
high-risk and high -density corridors on National Highways and State 
Highways, and at critical junctions at least in major cities with more than 
one million population (as per data available based on Million Plus Urban 
Agglomerations or Cities: c ensus of India 2011 or as per the latest 
census) including the 132 non -attainment cities (under National Clean 
Air Programme), and the electronic enforcement device shall be placed 
in such a manner so as not to cause any obstruction, line -of-sight issues 
or interruption in traffic flow. 
Provision of Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) is envisaged 
in high traffic density corridors which has provisions for CCTV/PTZ 
cameras, Variable message signs, Vehicle Actuated Speed Display 
System, Automatic Traffic Counter cum Classifier and Vid eo Incident 
Detection System, which help in speedy identification of    incidents and 
effective training on the highway stretches, thereby improving the 
response time of    the on-site assistance. The Provision    of ATMS has 
been included in the latest tende rs of majority of 4/6 laning projects of 
National Highways Authority of India. Presently fully functional ATMS 
system is available on Eastern Peripheral Expressway and Delhi Meerut 
Expressway.

 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether consumers are charged for replacing  dilapidated cables and electricity 
poles in the country; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has made any plan  to change the dilapidated cables and 
electricity poles in the country; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and the time by which it is likely to be implemented? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b)  :  Government of India  launched Deen  Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti  Yojana 
(DDUGJY) and Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS) in December, 2014 for 
various rural and urban electrificati on works respectively, which inter -alia comprised 
separation of agriculture and non -agriculture feeders, strengthening and augmentation 
of sub -transmission & distribution infrastructure, metering of distribution 
transformers/feeders/consumers and electrification of  villages across the country. 
 
Under DDUGJY and IPDS, reconductoring works were undertaken , which 
include replacing dilapidated cables and electricity poles, for which consumers were 
not charged  for grant portion given by Government of India .  Works under these 
schemes have been completed and the schemes stand closed on 31.03.2022.  
 
  Distribution companies also undertake repairs and maintenance at their 
level as permitted in tariff regulations of State Electricity Regulatory Commission.  
 
(c) & (d) : Government of India have also launched the Reforms Based Result Linked 
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) with an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 crore and 
an estimated GBS of Rs. 97,631 crore from Central Government. The Scheme seeks to 
improve the op erational efficiencies and financial sustainability of all DISCOMs/Power 
Departments excluding private DISCOMs by providing conditional financial assistance to 
DISCOMs for strengthening of supply infrastructure (including Distribution transformers, 
laying of new cables/lines, replacement of dilapidated cables and electricity poles etc.) 
based on meeting pre -qualifying criteria as well as upon achievement of basic minimum 
benchmarks by the DISCOMs evaluated on the basis of agreed evaluation framework 
tied to financial improvements. The States have been advised to pose their DPRs to the 
Ministry of Power in this regard and projects of most of the States have been 
sanctioned.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
Lok Sabha 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 2758 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  22nd December 2022 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF CALICUT INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT 
2758.    SHRI M.K. RAGHAVAN                       
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether the Government has any data regarding the number of seats 
available from Kozhikode and other International Airports of Kerala to 
other International destinations and if so the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether despite several pleas from Indian diaspora in GCC countries to 
increase number of seats to GCC countries, no action has been taken in 
this regard and if so the details therof including reasons for delay; 
 
(c) whether the Government has any data regarding the performance of 
Calicut International Airport compared to other airports of Kerala and if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has noticed that inspire of good performance, 
Calicut International Airport is neglected in terms of development and if 
so, the details pf the steps taken to improve infrastructure and bring in 
wide bodied aircraft to Calicut airport? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (GEN. 
(DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)) 
(a) Under the various Air Service Agreements concluded by India with 
foreign countries, seats or services are negotiated for the country as a 
whole and not on an airport-wise basis. Indian designated carriers are free 
to mount scheduled operations to/from any international/customs airport 
to foreign destinations under the ambit of bilateral Air Service Agreements 
as per mutually agreed capacity limits. The data on flight operations as 
per Winter schedule 2022 from international airports in Kerala is at 
Annexure A. 
 

(b) Operations of foreign airlines are governed by bilateral Air Services 
Agreement (ASA) between India and the respective country (which has 
designated the airline). Any foreign airline can operate to/from a point 
(airport) in India if it is designated as a point of call in the ASA. At present, 
the Government of India follows a policy of promoting more international 
operations by Indian carriers from non-metro points either directly or 
through their own domestic operations. Accordingly, to support the Indian 
carriers, the policy is to not grant any non-metro airport as a new point of 
call in the ASAs to any foreign carrier. 
 
    In accordance with Air Services Agreements (ASA), Indian designated 
carriers are free to mount operations to/from any international airport 
including Kozhikode to foreign destinations under the ambit of bilateral air 
service agreements concluded by India with foreign countries as per 
mutually agreed capacity limits.   
 
 It may also be noted that Kozhikode, Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram 
airports are already included in the list of 18 tourist gateway destinations 
from where the Indian carriers and carriers of 5 SAARC countries 
(Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Maldives and Sri Lanka) and 10 ASEAN 
countries (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Indonesia, 
Myanmar, Cambodia, Philippines and Laos) can operate unlimited 
frequencies subject to availability of slots at the airport. As such, the 
government has provided an enabling environment for growth of civil 
aviation sector but does not interfere in the operational plans of the 
airlines.  
 
    Airlines are free to select whatever markets and network they wish to 
service and operate within the ambit of bilateral agreements. The airlines 
provide air services to specific places depending upon the traffic demand 
and commercial viability. ; 
 
(c) The State of Kerala has Kozhikode, Kannur, Thiruvananthapuram and 
Cochin International Airports. The comparison of flight movements, 
footfall and freight movement at these airports is at Annexure B.; 
 
(d) In August 2020 an Air India Express flight met with an accident at 
Kozhikode airport. Consequently, the commercial wide-body operations 
were suspended by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) 
pending investigation by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau 
(AAIB). The AAIB which conducted the investigation made certain 
recommendations with regard to Kozhikode airport.; 

 
     A Committee of aviation experts was constituted by the Ministry of 
Civil Aviation to oversee the implementation of the recommendations 
made in the report of the investigation conducted by AAIB and the 
execution of the steps required for implementation of these 
recommendations. One of the mandates of the Committee was to study 
the feasibility of operation of Wide Body aircraft at Kozhikode airport and 
to give its recommendations thereon. The Committee recommended that 
Code D and Code E aircraft operations may remain suspended till such 
time that all recommendations and additional recommendations accepted 
by the Committee along with mitigation measures for safe Code C aircraft 
operations are put in place. As such, the commercial operations of Wide 
Bodied aircraft from Kozhikode airport are presently suspended. 
 
     One of the recommendations of the Committee was for providing 
Runway End Safety Area (RESA) at both ends of the runway at Kozhikode 
airport as per the extant provisions. This Ministry has requested Kerala 
Government to provide stabilized leveled land for runway expansion at 
Kozhikode airport. Details such as the timelines for handing over the land, 
methodology of costing, cost etc. were requested from the State 
Government, which are yet to be received. The resumption of Code D and 
Code E operations from Kozhikode is dependent on the requested land 
being made available by the State government.
